name: Jukha
description: Jukha is a high-speed Israeli-Bulgarian 'hot potato' game where players compete to empty their hands by matching cards while avoiding (or passing) the unique Joker. It is a game of reflexes and nerve, as the Joker acts as a barrier to victory. It is almost identical in mechanics to the Bulgarian 'Joker' game but with specific variations in the 'Final Duel'.

content.text: Jukha is a high-speed Israeli-Bulgarian 'hot potato' game where players compete to empty their hands by matching cards while avoiding (or passing) the unique Joker. It is a game of reflexes and nerve, as the Joker acts as a barrier to victory. It is almost identical in mechanics to the Bulgarian 'Joker' game but with specific variations in the 'Final Duel'.

Rooted in the Sephardic and Mizrahi communities in Israel who brought 'passing' games from the Balkans and Turkey. The name 'Jukha' (or 'Juxa') is a common moniker for the Joker card in these regions.
Dealer shuffles and deals all cards out. If players have unequal counts, it is accepted as part of the game.

items.text: Single loser: As soon as any player exits, play ends and the player holding the joker is the loser (may have been the original rule).
Last two lose: When only two players remain, the player holding the joker is the loser.
Double out: When only two players remain they compete in a final duel; both are losers unless one exits (regional variant).
